analysis:
No concrete security regression is visible in the supplied files.

CHANGELOG.md (head lines 1027-1771) is documentation only. It describes SSD prefix-cache work, profiler telemetry and provider release notes, and changes no code or trust policy. Its claims that touch T-041 (SSD cache), T-051 (profiler) and T-003 (hop-by-hop plaintext) match the canonical threat model. I did not independently verify them against the code. The changelog statements about 100 GiB default SSD cache ceiling and 'half of available space' may differ from the threat model's 'no fixed ceiling' wording. That is a documentation-consistency question, not a code finding.

coordinator/api/inference/admission.go (head lines 38-39) adds two optional fields to AdmissionRequest: FallbackDeadline (time.Duration) and DeadlineForWork (func(string, *protocol.PromptWork) time.Duration). They are data-only and are not consumed anywhere in the supplied diff. Admission and routing behaviour is unchanged in the supplied code.

coordinator/api/inference/alias_planner.go (patch, new lines about 17-19) adds Owner.maybeFallbackAliasWithDeadline. It is a thin wrapper that forwards to routeplan.AliasPlanner.FallbackWithDeadline with the same arguments. It adds no authorization, billing or encryption logic.

Coverage limits for later passes:
- The routeplan implementation of FallbackWithDeadline and any callers of the new fields or wrapper are not in this batch.
- The next pass should check whether DeadlineForWork or FallbackDeadline can be derived from consumer-controlled input and so shorten or extend the first-content deadline. Relevant threats are DoS or billing and refund correctness around RefundReservation.
- It should also check that alias fallback keeps per-model eligibility, cache scope, and provider-body error checks (ProviderBodyErrorForModel, CachePlanForModel) consistent.
